papers.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
papers.summary: The authors describe hypothesis generation, experimental execution, analysis and manuscript preparation with an experiment-manager agent and progressive tree search.
papers.relevance: Separate experiment management, evidence analysis and review rather than equating successful code execution with scientific discovery.
limitations: Author-reported results from this paper do not validate this lab's implementation.
A workflow resemblance does not establish novelty or a replicated scientific capability.

papers.title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
papers.summary: The framework develops a human-supplied idea through literature review, experimentation and report writing with opportunities for researcher feedback.
papers.relevance: Use bounded specialist work orders and retain human review at scientific and publication decisions.
limitations: Only the primary abstract and metadata were reviewed here.
The paper's model and cost findings are not measurements of Research Lab OS.

papers.title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
papers.summary: The benchmark evaluates agents performing machine-learning experiments across diverse tasks; its abstract reports large differences in success across tasks and challenges in planning and hallucination.
papers.relevance: Evaluate an end-to-end research workflow on multiple independent tasks; retain negative outcomes and inspectable action records.
limitations: This catalog does not reproduce the benchmark.
An engineering fixture cannot establish general research-agent competence.
